plain: Words used to move or persuade people, often in a showy way

webster.text: The art of speaking with propriety, elegance and force.

example.quote: But the rhetoric of the gentleman has highly colored the dangers of giving the general government an indefinite power of providing for the general welfare.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 3, Virginia Convention, June 17, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
